title: Malware Threats

objectives.text: Tell a virus, worm, Trojan, rootkit, backdoor, bot, spyware, logic bomb and ransomware apart from their behavior
Name the parts of a malware kit (dropper, downloader, packer, crypter, wrapper, payload) and the common infection vectors
Describe what makes a threat an APT and put the APT lifecycle stages in order
Explain how fileless malware uses native tools, memory and the registry or WMI, and which controls see it (AMSI, script block logging, EDR)
Explain what AI changes for malware authors and defenders, including runtime LLM use, polymorphism and attacks on ML detectors
Separate static from dynamic analysis and match each step to its tool (hashing, strings, packing, PE imports, Process Monitor, Autoruns, Sysmon)
Set up a safe analysis lab and turn findings into indicators and YARA rules
Choose layered countermeasures for a malware scenario and decide when to rebuild a host instead of cleaning it

readingMap.why: Most malware questions are type identification from a short description; learn the defining trait of each type and the APT lifecycle order.
Short section, but fileless and living-off-the-land scenarios are common and link to the detection tools.
New in v13: know what AI changes and the detection answer; skip vendor product detail.
Static vs dynamic and tool-to-task matching are frequent tool-identification questions.
Scenario questions ask for the best control; learn the virus detection methods and the rebuild rule.

labs.name: Hash, look up and inspect a harmless test file
labs.skill: Static analysis basics on the EICAR test file in your own VM: SHA-256 hash, VirusTotal hash lookup, Strings, and watching your antivirus react

labs.name: Write and test a YARA rule against your own files
labs.skill: Rule structure (meta, strings, condition) and matching a family by stable features instead of a hash

labs.name: Baseline autostarts and process activity with Sysinternals on your own PC
labs.skill: Reading Autoruns, Process Monitor and TCPView output the way a dynamic analysis does, on a clean system

labs.name: Map a #StopRansomware advisory to ATT&CK and pick the countermeasures
labs.skill: Turning a real ransomware report into techniques (T1486, T1490, T1566) and matching controls

feynmanPrompts: Explain to a friend the difference between a virus, a worm and a Trojan using one everyday example for each, then say which one WannaCry was and why.
Walk through how fileless malware can run without dropping a program file, and explain why AMSI and script block logging still catch it.
Describe how you would analyze an unknown attachment safely, from lab setup to a YARA rule, and say which steps are static and which are dynamic.
